questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For a long time I had a dream about living in Norway, to explore the country, culture and the nature close by, so an exchange in Oslo was perfect for me. They also had some very interesting courses, that was different from what UCPH could offer me.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I just loved it

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The website of University of Oslo was very informative with every aspect of the proces, and if I didn't find my answers here, they always wrote who I should contact to get my answers. They were always very quick to answer my emails.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was arranged a buddy week, where we were introduced to the University, the city, the culture and spend time in our buddy groups with other students from the faculty and attended activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Super easy. The website of University of Oslo recommended me to apply for student housing at SiO, and it was super easy. In my application I had to prioritize six different types of student housing, and I recieved an offer short time after my application.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It's great! I can really recommend renting student housing through SiO, and especially to apply for Sogn Studentby. We were so many exchange students, and it felt like our own little town. The area is a grat location for meeting people and making friends, there is even a Rema 1000 and a student pub (Amatøren) in the area!

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I lived in a shared flat with six other people from different countries in Europe, and even though were were all quite different, it really worked out well. I can recommend taking initiative to make Sunday dinners together, card game nights, hiking trips or other things so you get to know each other. Since we all shared the same kitchen and bathroom/toilet, I can also recommend making a cleaning plan for the different months of the semester - sounds boring, but it makes living together more easy and without bad vibes from living in a dirty flat haha.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Overall it was pretty smooth. Sometimes it was a bit confusing with the application process for some of the courses, as I wanted to apply for some that either weren't a part of the exchange courses or at another faculty. But everything worked out in the end, and they were quick at answering my e-mails.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Contacting the faculty or the faculty's responsible person for exchange students over e-mail.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: During my buddy/introduction week I had to make some changes in my courses, as i didn't get into one that I wanted. But then I just looked in the course catalog from the website of University of Oslo once again, and applied for some other ones, and got a spot on the new one I wanted.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Start early with making your own overview on, what you should apply for (registration at the university, courses, housing etc.) and when, so you are aware of important deadlines. Also remember to check your KU-mail daily during the proces.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: They were great! I found them very relevant for both my studies and my personal interests, and I have the experience that I graduated feeling much more aware of patterns and developments in our society.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Maybe a bit more individual work at UiO compared to UCPH that often had obligatory assignments or exams in groups. Other than that I would say it is quite similar to UCPH.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
MEVIT1320 – Journalistikkens rolle, etikk og nyhetsproduksjon i det moderne samfunnet
MEVIT3117 – Contemporary TV fiction
NOR2415 – Contemporary Scandinavian Film: Cultural, Aesthetic and Literary Approaches

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: MEVIT1320 gave me a great understanding of tendencies in news making, and which dilemmas and ethical questions journalism is facing in order to keep our interest and attention in a media landscape characterized by algorithms, mis- and desinformation.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food and restaurants were more expensive

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Explore the nature! Go out hiking, skiing or cabin trips! Oslo has so much to offer

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: University of Oslo has a bunch of associations to attend. Some cost money (like sport associations) but it varies how much the amount is. I joined the knitting association and it was only 50 NOK for the whole semester

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The knitting association was cute. Some of my friends also joined the choir and had a really nice time with that!

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: HIKING! Take the T-bane up to Vettakollen and hike to the beautiful viewpoint over the city. Hike to the different cabins that offer delicious cinnamon buns - i recommend Tryvann Sportsstua or Ullevål Seter sportsstua. Buy a membership at DNT (Den norkse turistforening) and rent a cabin for a cabin trip.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Easy as it is not too different from the danish culture.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The local students can be quite reserved. I recommend joining an association with local students, so you meet them in another context than only in the courses.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The nature. Even though Oslo is the capital of Norway, I was surprised of how easy it was to get out in the nature within short time. It is such a big part of the everyday life of the Norwegians. I always saw people walking to school, in the metro or just around in the city carrying their hiking gear or cross country skiis. It was cute and I felt like a true norwegian when I also went hiking or on cabin trips like they do. Wherever you are in the city you are always guaranteed to see mountains or beautiful fjords in the horizon. I loved it.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Everything I already mentioned and recommended. Take initiative, be spontaneous and try out new things. You are only there for a short time, so make the most out of it as you can. Carpe diem<3

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: The Erasmus scholarship was crucial for my exchange, but I can also recommend applying for other scholarships so you don't have to worry about your expences

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Getting a fresh start in a foreign country, exploring the city and the culture and of course making really (!) great friends that I will miss so much

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Making time for all the stuff and trips I wanted to do

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
